markup: How does the perihelion and aphelion position of the earth take place?

markup: Differentiate between : Cyclones and Anticyclones

markup: Importance of soil in plant growth
answermarkup:

markup: Apogee
answermarkup:
i) Moon revolves around the Earth in an elliptical orbit. Hence the distance between the earth and the moon varies.

markup: Apparent movement of sun
answermarkup:
i. The position of the sun on the horizon at sunrise and sunset appears to change everyday. However, in reality the sun does not change its position.
ii. This happens due to the revolution of the earth around the sun and the inclination of the earth's axis.
iii. The period from 21st  June to 22nd  December, when the position of the rising sun appears to shift towards the south, is called as Dakshinayan.
iv. The period from 22nd  December to 21st  June, when the position of the rising sun appears to shift towards the north, is called as Uttarayan.

markup: Importance of soil in human civilization
answermarkup:
i. Man has been using soil as a resource to obtain agricultural produce, since ancient time.
ii. He eventually realized that fertile soils along the river beds give higher yields, which led humans to settle in the valleys and live in groups.
iii. This gave rise to the ancient river valley civilizations like the Indus Valley civilization.
iv. As the population grew, man started producing more crops.
v. For a higher production, fertile soil and availability of water were required. As a result, there was a competition to discover the fertile lands and settle there.
vi. In order to further increase the production, man made use of different fertilizers which led to record agricultural productions.

markup: Total Lunar Eclipse
answermarkup:
i) Lunar eclipse occurs when the moon enters the earth's shadow while revolving around it.
ii) For a lunar eclipse to occur, the earth should be between the sun and the moon and all three of them should be in the same line and in the same plane.
iii) As the path of moon's revolution passes through the thick shadow of the earth, the moon gets completely hidden in this shadow. As a result, a total lunar eclipse occurs.
iv) The maximum duration of a total lunar eclipse is 107 minutes.

markup: Effects of seasons on the living world.
answermarkup:
i. Different season occur on earth due to the revolution of the earth around the sun and the inclination of the earth's axis.
ii. This results in diversity on earth and affects the life on the earth.
iii. The region in the North Pole and the South Pole receives sunlight only for few months of the year. Even in this period, certain flora and fauna develops in this region.
iv. Penguins, seal and walruses are found in the Antarctic region in the southernmost part of earth, while animals like reindeer, polar bears, Artic foxes are found in the Arctic region in the nothernmost part.
v. People and living things adapt to the climatic conditions in their respective regions.
vi. However, this adaptation is possible only upto a certain limit and organisms prefer a certain habitat.
vii. Number of birds temporarily migrate to other regions during extreme cold climatic condition when food is also scarce. Trees also bear fruits only in a particular season.
viii. Occupations of humans like agriculture are also dependent on seasons.

markup: Measures of soil conservation
answermarkup:
Considering the importance of soils for occupations like agriculture, it is extremely important to conserve soil and protect the fertile soils of the farmlands from getting washed away.
To prevent the soil erosion due to rain water and wind, the following measures have been suggested / adopted:
i. Government of Maharashtra has implemented 'the catchment area development program'. As per the program, the following measures for conservation of soil were undertaken:
a. Constructing embankments along the slopes in rural areas:
This checks the velocity of the water down the slopes and reduces soil erosion.
Moreover, planting trees can also control the velocity of winds, thereby reducing the erosion of soil by wind. Also, the roots hold the soil in place and reduce the erosion.
b. Introducing Continuous Contour Trenches (CCTs) along the steep slopes:
Constructing Continuous Contour Trenches (CCTs) along the steep slopes at different heights helps check the velocity of running water down these slopes and, thereby reduces the soil erosion.
ii. These measures led to the success of the 'Arrest water, let it percolate' scheme, which resulted in reduced soil erosion and also raised the ground-water level.
iii. Also, under the recently launched scheme, Jalayukt Shivar, the following measures are undertaken:
a. Construction of farm bunds
b. Arresting waters of small streams
c. Connecting the streams
iv. A regular use of organic manures and vermicompost helps to maintain the pH level of the soil, increases the proportion of humus in the soil and retains its fertility.

markup: Intertidal range
answermarkup:
i) The difference between the water levels of the high and low tides is called as the tidal range.
ii) In open seas, this range is about 30 cm but goes on increasing towards the coastal areas.
iii) For the most part of the coast of Peninsular India, this range is around 100 to 150 cm.
iv) The highest tidal range in the world is 1600 cm and is at the Bay of Fundy along the Atlantic coast of North America.
v) The highest tidal range in the India is 1100 cm and is at the Gulf of Khambat.

markup: Annular Solar Eclipse
answermarkup:
i) As the moon revolves around the earth in an elliptical orbit, the distance between the earth and the moon varies.
ii) During a solar eclipse, when the moon is in the apogee position i.e. the farthest from the earth, its deep shadow is cast in space and does not reach the earth.
iii) At this time, only an illuminated edge of the sun is seen in the form of a ring, from a very limited portion of the earth. This is called as annular solar eclipse.
iv) Annular solar eclipse is a rare phenomenon.

markup: Contour Maps

iv) Help in identifying hills, valleys, and drainage patterns.

markup: Horizontal distribution of air pressure
answermarkup:
i) Temperature and air pressure are inter-related.
ii) When the temperature is high, a low pressure belt is formed. Conversely, when the temperature is low, a high pressure belt is formed.
iii) Also, there is uneven distribution of sunrays as the earth's curvature starts increasing as we go from the equator towards the poles. This leads to uneven distribution of temperature on the earth's surface.
iv) This uneven distribution of temperature results in the formation of low and high pressure belts horizontally between the equator and the poles, in both the hemispheres.

3) Man is thinking of constructing colonies on other planets and their satellites, too, in future.

markup: Spring tide
answermarkup:
i) On new moon and full moon days, the gravitational pulls of the sun and the moon act on the earth in the same direction and hence, the total pull increases. Therefore, the tides are much higher than the average high tides.
ii) As the bulge at the high tide is greater, the level of the low tide recedes farther than usual. As a result, the water level is higher than the usual high tide and lower than the usual low tide. This is called as Spring tide.

markup: Agrotourism

iv. Agrotourism is financially beneficial for the farmer and his village.

markup: Place where you will get the information about the suitability of a soil for a particular crop.

markup: Write a note on 'typhoons'.
answermarkup:
The cyclones occurring in the western part of the Pacific Ocean along the coasts of Japan, China, Philippines, etc. are called as 'Typhoons'. In certain regions, cyclones get destructive and take the form of a storm. They are called as cyclonic storms. Typhoon is an example of a cyclonic storm.
They arise in the months between June and October.
They have high velocity winds and cause heavy rainfalls, making them destructive in nature.

markup: Nucleated Settlements

markup: Neap tide
answermarkup:
i) While revolving around the earth, the moon makes a right angle with respect to the sun and the moon. This happens twice a month i.e. on the first and the third quarter days of each month.
ii) On both these days, the forces of the sun and the moon operate at right angles on the earth.
iii) At the places where the sun causes a high tide, the gravitational pull of the moon which is at right angle also acts on the sea water. Due to such conditions, the rise of sea water level is less than usual at the time of high tide. Whereas, the fall in sea water level is less than usual at the time of low tide. This is called as Neap tide.

markup: How are cyclones named?
answermarkup:
Cyclones occurring in different parts of the world are assigned different names.
A list of names is prepared for a particular ocean or a particular part of an ocean.
The names in this list are suggested by the countries around that particular ocean.
If the speed of the winds exceeds 33 knots or 60 km per hour, a cyclone is assigned a name. This is done to make it easier for us to remember the storm.

markup: Organic Farming
answermarkup:
i. The farming done using all the vestal matter mixed in the soil is known as organic farming.
ii. Chemical fertilizers and pesticides are not used in this type of farming.
iii. When the nutrients of the soil get used up by the crop, it needs to be replenished. Also, additional nutrients are required to increase the yield of the crop.
iv. Organic fertilizers are prepared for replenishing the nutrient level of the soil, by the following methods:
a. Decomposing the litter in the ground
b. Burying grasses like sesbania or jute in the soil for making manures
c. Using cowdung or compost manures
d. Obtaining vermicompost from organic waste
v. Also, organic pesticides like neem are used for controlling the pests.
vi. The crop obtained from organic farming is high in quality.

markup: Organic Manures
answermarkup:
i. Organic manure is necessary to turn the weathered powdery rock into soil.
ii. It comes from the decomposition of organic matter like the remains of plants and animals, vegetal litters, roots of plants, etc.
iii. Organic matter like remains of plants and animals are continuously decomposed by microorganisms and certain other organisms while organic matter like vegetal litters, roots of plants, etc. get decomposed by water.
iv. This organic manure then gets mixed in the soil and produces humus, which makes the soil fertile.
v. Now-a-days, vermicompost is produced on a large scale. Its production requires sufficient period of time, organic waste, water, heat, etc.

markup: Perigee
answermarkup:
i) Moon revolves around the Earth in an elliptical orbit. Hence the distance between the earth and the moon varies.
ii) The position when the moon is closest to the Earth is called as perigee.
iii) In the perigee position, the moon is 3,56,000 km away from the earth.

markup: Occultation
answermarkup:
i) While revolving around the earth, the moon sometimes obscures a star or a planet and that celestial body appears to be hidden behind the moon. This process is called as occultation.
ii) It is an astronomical event and occurs with reference to the moon.
iii) This kind of occultation can be seen during a total solar eclipse or annular solar eclipse when the sun disc gets hidden completely because of the moon.

markup: Market Gardening
answermarkup:
i. Market gardening is a type of cultivation developed as a result of urbanization and the ready markets available in urban centres.
ii. This type of cultivation works on the economic principle of supply and demand.
iii. The land holding in this type of cultivation is small.
iv. The main characteristics of this type of farming include the use of irrigation, organic and chemical fertilizers, low investment, use of manpower, demand of markets, use of science and technology, etc.
v. Since, the quality and price of the product is dependent on rapid transport, this type of farming is also known as 'truck farming'.

markup: Partial lunar eclipse
answermarkup:
i) Lunar eclipse occurs when the moon enters the earth's shadow while revolving around it.
ii) For a lunar eclipse to occur, the earth should be between the sun and the moon and all three of them should be in the same line and in the same plane.
iii) While the path of moon's revolution passes through the earth's shadow, if only a part of the moon gets hidden in this shadow, a partial lunar eclipse occurs.

markup: Geographic Indication (GI)
answermarkup:
i. Certain soils are best suited for only a certain type of crops.
ii. As a result, the production of that crop becomes the speciality of that soil and consequently, of that area.
iii. Such crops are given the status of Geographic Indication (GI).
e.g.: Haapus mango from Sindhudurg, custard apple from Beed district and oranges from Nagpur.

markup: Animal life and human life in hot desert region.
answermarkup:
i) The climate of hot desert region consists of tremendous heat and very low rainfall. Also the nights are very cold.
ii) Due to such climatic conditions, animals like camel which can survive without water for many days are found here.
iii) Animals live inside the ground during daytime and the number of animals living on ground is less. They include snake, rats, lizards, scorpions, etc.
iv) Domesticated animals like horse, donkeys, sheep, oxen, etc. are also found.
v) People in this region fulfill most of their requirement from animals and agriculture is carried out only near river valleys and oases.
vi) Bedoins from Sahara desert, Bushmen from Kalahari and Aborigines from Australia are some of the tribes found in hot desert region.

markup: Give information : Rural settlements and cultural stability
answermarkup:
1) Rural settlement is the first step towards a stable life in human history. 
2) The process of growth and expansion of settlements begin in rural settlements. Gradually, the rural settlements get transformed into urban settlements. 
3) The life in urban settlements is more dynamic. On the other hand the life in rural settlement is comparatively traditional. Thus, rural settlements preserves the cultural stability.

markup: Taiga region
answermarkup:
i) Taiga region lies approximately between 55° and 65° N. parallel in the interior parts of the continents.
ii) The summer temperature in this region is about 15° to 20° C while the winter temperature is below 0° C.
iii) It rains in summer and the mean annual rainfall is around 300 to 500 mm. It snows in winter in this region.
iv) Vegetation here consists of coniferous forests, with trees having narrow and pointed leaves, branches leaning towards the ground and light and soft wood.
v) Spruce, fir, pine, redwood, etc. are some of the trees found in this region.
vi) Animals with soft and thick fur like caribous, elks, ermine, beavers, silver fox, minks, bears, etc. are found in this region.
vii) The population of this region is less and hunting and lumbering are major occupations. Few agrarian activities are also carried out.
viii) Taiga region extends from Alaska to the Atlantic coast and in some parts of Eurasia.

markup: Give information : Factors influencing the location of human settlements
answermarkup:
1) Physical, cultural and economic factors influence the location of human settlements. 
2) Physical factors like physiography, land/soils, climate, water supply, river banks, etc. influence the location of human settlement. 
3) The cultural factors like defense, health, education, tourism, historical significance, etc. also affect the location of human settlements. (4) The economic factors like irrigation, occupations, transport and communication, industries, trade, government offices, etc. have their impact on the location of human settlements.

markup: Mid-latitudinal high pressure belts
answermarkup:
i) Mid-latitudinal high pressure belts are formed between 25° to 35° parallels in both the hemispheres.
ii) The heated and lighter air from the equatorial region starts ascending.
iii) After reaching the higher altitudes, it moves towards the polar regions.
iv) The low temperatures in these regions cools the air down and make it heavier. This heavier air descends down in both the hemispheres creating high pressure belts.
v) As this air is dry, this region does not get rainfall. Hence, most of the hot deserts on the earth are found in this region.

markup: Reason for using contour maps in hilly regions.
answermarkup:
i) Show the height and shape of hills clearly.
ii) Help in finding safe routes for mountaineering.
iii) Indicate steep and gentle slopes accurately.
iv) Assist in planning construction and road networks.

markup: People practicing shifting cultivation also undertake other activities in forests.
answermarkup:
i. In shifting cultivation type of farming, the production obtained is not sufficient to fulfill the food requirement.
ii. The fallow period in this type of farming is longer than the crop period.
iii. Also, the productivity of the land depletes in two or three years and a different piece of land needs to be selected for farming.
Hence, people practicing shifting cultivation also undertake other activities like hunting, fishing and gathering of bulbs and roots from forests.

markup: Rural settlements develop near natural resources.
answermarkup:
i) Early human life depended directly on water, fertile soil and forests for survival.
ii) Agriculture, fishing and hunting require immediate access to natural resources.
iii) Availability of food and livelihood makes people settle permanently in such areas.
iv) These conditions support stable living, leading to the growth of rural settlements.

markup: Any object on the surface of the earth remains at the place where it exists.
answermarkup:
i) The force that the earth gets by the virtue of its rotation is called as centrifugal force. It acts away from the centre of the earth.
ii) Due to this force, any object on the earth would be thrown into the space.
iii) However, the earth's gravitational force, which is many times greater than its centrifugal force, acts towards the centre of the earth at the same time causing the object on the surface of the earth to remain stable at its place.
Hence, any object on the surface of the earth remains at the place where it exists.

markup: The moon appears semicircular on the first and the third quarter days?
answermarkup:
i) The illuminated parts of the moon that are visible from earth are called phases of the moon.
ii) These phases are visible due to the sunlight reflected from the moon's surface.
iii) On the first and the third quarter days, the sun, the earth and the moon make relative angle of 90°. On these two days, only half part of the moon gets illuminated.
Hence, the moon appears semicircular on the first and the third quarter days.

markup: Lunar eclipse does not occur on every full moon day.
answermarkup:
i) Lunar eclipse occurs when the moon enters the earth's shadow while revolving around it.
ii) It usually occurs on a full moon day.
iii) For a lunar eclipse to occur, it is necessary that the moon, the earth and the sun fall in one line and also in the same plane.
iv) However, this does not happen on every full moon day. Hence, lunar eclipse does not occur on every full moon day.

markup: Why scattered settlements are found in high relief areas.
answermarkup:
i) Few houses are needed due to limited population.
ii) Terrains are difficult to build large villages.
iii) Dependence on nearby villages for daily needs.
iv) Close to natural resources like forests or pastures.

markup: Linear settlements are seen along roads and rivers.
answermarkup:
i) Roads and rivers provide easy transport and communication.
ii) People prefer building houses along long routes for accessibility.
iii) Shops and services grow along these routes, extending the settlement.
iv) Economic activities increase as movement of people and goods becomes easier.

markup: Soil formation process is faster in the equatorial climate.
answermarkup:
1) High temperatures and high rainfall are the main features of equatorial climate. 
2) The temperature of Equatorial region is around 27°C to 30°C throughout the year. 
3) The mean annual rainfall in Equatorial region is around 2500 mm to 3000 mm . It rains throughout the year in this region. 
4) In the region of high temperatures and high rainfall, the process of soil formation is faster. Thus, due to high temperatures and high rainfall, soil formation process is faster in the equatorial climate.

markup: Reason why contour lines are important for understanding landforms.
answermarkup:
i) Show altitude differences between areas.
ii) Help in identifying hills, valleys, and slopes.
iii) Aid in planning trekking or construction activities.
iv) Assist in flood and soil erosion management.

markup: Humus content in the soil increases.
answermarkup:
1) The regular use of organic manures, vermicompost, compost helps in maintaining the pH balance in the soil. 
2) A large number of microorganisms exist in the soil with high pH . 
3) Microorganisms decompose the dead remains of the plants and animals and other organic materials. The biotic material thus produed is call humus. Thus, by regular use of organic manures, humus content in the soil increases.

markup: Air pressure decreases with increasing altitude.
answermarkup:
i) The altitude of a region is one of the factors influencing the air pressure.
ii) Near the earth's surface, the proportion of dust particles, water vapour, heavy gases, etc. in the air is more.
iii) This proportion decreases as the altitude increases. Due to which, as one moves higher, the air gets thinner.
As a result, air pressure decreases with increasing altitude.

markup: Houses are built and different facilities develop in rural settlements.
answermarkup:
a. The settlements where the original occupations of majority of the people are based on natural resources are known as rural settlements.
b. Over a period of time, other associated occupations gradually develop in these settlements.
c. As a result, people from surrounding areas migrate and settle in these areas.
d. This leads to the building of houses and developments of different facilities in rural settlements.

markup: Human settlements get concentrated in the areas having fertile soil.
answermarkup:
i. Higher agricultural yields can be obtained in areas with fertile soils.
ii. Regions where soils are fertile and arable are self-reliant as far as the food production is concerned.
iii. On the other hand, regions where soil is not arable have to import food to fulfil their food requirements.
iv. Agro-based industries also flourish in such areas and show signs of development.
Hence, human settlements get concentrated in the areas with fertile soil.

markup: Duration of day and night changes throughout the year
answermarkup:
i) The tilt of the Earth’s axis remains constant.

markup: Write in detail about the factors necessary for soil formation.
answermarkup:
The parent rock, the climate of the region, the biotic material, the slope of the land and time are the necessary factors for soil formation. These factors together influence the process of soil formation. Their detailed information is as follows :
1) Parent rock : Parent rock in a region is an important factor in soil formation. Depending on the hardness of the parent rock and the climate of the region, the parent rock gets weathered. The rock turns into powdery material which further turns into earthy material. For example, (i) The besalt rock of the Deccan Plateau in Maharashtra turns into black soil after weathering. Black soil is also referred to as 'regur' soil. (ii) Rocks like granite or gneiss in South India give rise to red soil.
2) Regional climate : The intensity of weathering of rock depends on the climate of the region. The same type of rock gives rise to different types of soils when it is exposed to different climates. For example, In dry climate of Deccan Plateau, weathering of basalt leads to the formation of black soil whereas, in the humid climate of the Western Sahyadris, the leaching of the same basalt rock leads to the formation of lateritic soil.
3) Biotic material : The biotic material comes from the decomposition of the remains of the plants and animals in a particular region. Many microorganisms and certain other organisms help in decomposition process. The decomposed biotic material gets mixed into the soils and is called humus. If the proportion of humus in the soil is greater, the soils become fertile.
4) Time : Soil formation is a natural and slow process. To form a 2.5 cm thick layer of top soil, it takes thousands of years. In the region of high rainfall and higher temperatures, the process of soil formation is faster. On the other hand, in the region of low rainfall and low temperatures, the process of soil formation takes more time.

markup: What effect does temperature have on air pressure?

ii) As the temperature increases, air pressure decreases and vice versa.

markup: When total solar eclipse occurs, why partial solar eclipse is also seen from the earth?
answermarkup:
i) On a new moon day, if the sun, the moon and the earth fall in one line and are also in the same plane then a solar eclipse occurs. It happens because the moon's shadow falls on the earth.
ii) This shadow is of two types - the central shadow and the peripheral shadow. The central portion is darker and the periphery is light.
iii) In the area of the earth where the dark shadow falls, the sun becomes completely invisible. Such an area experiences a total solar eclipse.
iv) Whereas, at the same time, at the places where the shadow is lighter, the sun disc appears partially covered. Such an area experiences a partial solar eclipse.
Hence, we experience total solar eclipse and partial solar eclipse simultaneously on earth.

markup: Explain the characteristics of shifting cultivation.
answermarkup:
The characteristics of shifting cultivation are as follows :
(1) Nature : Shifting cultivation is one subtype of traditional farming. It is a primitive type of cultivation.
(2) Methods : In shifting cultivation, every year a new area is choosen for cultivation. After a specific period of time, old areas are again used for cultivation. In this type of farming, the farmer initially selects a piece of land in the forest. In order to make it cultivable, he clears the land by cutting down the trees, plants, removing the shrubs and grass. Once the trees dry out, he burns them. The left over ash gets mixed in soil and acts as manure. Sowing and harvesting is done before the rainy season.
(3) Crop period and fallow period : In this type of farming, the fallow period is longer than the crop period. After the productivity of land depletes in two to three years, a different piece of land is selected for cultivation.
(4) Amount of production : The production obtained from this type of production is not sufficient to fulfil the food requirement. Hence people involved in this type of farming also undertakes hunting, fishing and gathering bulbs and roots from forests.

markup: How does a high pressure belt get formed near 30° parallel? Why does this region have hot deserts?

i) Mid-latitudinal high pressure belts are formed between 25° to 35° parallels in both the hemispheres.
ii) The heated air from the Equatorial low pressure belts becomes lighter and starts ascending. 
iii) After reaching higher altitudes, it starts moving towards the polar regions in both the hemispheres. 
iv) Due to the low temperatures in these regions, this air cools down, becomes heavier and descends. This leads to the formation of high pressure belts near 30° parallel.
As this air is dry, this region does not get rainfall. Hence, this region has hot deserts.

iii. On 21st  June, the north pole of the earth is tilted towards the sun and the sunrays become perpendicular on the Tropic of Cancer in the northern hemisphere. On this day, the circle of illumination divides the equator in two equal parts, as shown in the figure. It is summer season in the northern hemisphere and winter in the southern hemisphere.
iv. Similarly, on 22nd  December the south pole of the earth is tilted towards the sun and the sunrays become perpendicular on the Tropic of Capricorn in the southern hemisphere. On this day also the circle of illumination divides the equator in two equal parts. It is summer season in the southern hemisphere and winter in the northern hemisphere.
Thus, we can see that the climate in the equatorial region is almost same in all the cases and hence the effect of the seasons is not experienced in the equatorial region.
